sources.title: FIFA 2026 official media-licensee roster, June 11 revision
sources.notes: Official PDF, pages 10–13. Supersedes the June 3 mirror discovered in preparation. Luxembourg absent; absence is not proof of no licensed coverage. TV/digital license chain only in the condensed market table; radio remains in the original.

sources.title: ZDF tournament audience release, July 20
sources.notes: First-party ZDF release syndicated by Presseportal. Television match averages; age and consolidation detail not supplied. Keep separate from other providers and platforms.

sources.title: TVP tournament audience release, July 21
sources.notes: Nielsen Media AMR, consolidated+2 plus out-of-home. Gemius online users are a different metric, not added to TV AMR.

sources.title: Czech Television tournament audience release, July 20
sources.notes: ATO-Nielsen, 4+, Live+TS0-3 BS, PEM-D, GA as stated by publisher. TV averages separate from digital starts; selective published fixtures.

sources.title: NOS tournament audience release, July 21
sources.notes: 14 million reach includes matches and surrounding programmes. Definitive delayed/online figures pending in this release; no complete match panel. Provider/universe not supplied in the release.

sources.title: VRT tournament impact, July 27
sources.notes: Flemish community, not all Belgium; VRT evening-match average and selected Belgium fixture. Incompatible with an all-Belgium swarm denominator for a country audience ratio.

sources.title: Yle final audience, July 20
sources.notes: Around 1.5 million average and 2.1 million reach; platform composition of average and provider/universe insufficiently specified. 52 matches each for Yle and MTV confirms actual post-expansion coverage.

sources.title: SVT tournament viewing, July 24
sources.notes: 3.4 million SVT Play viewers, over 6 million combined SVT linear/Play reach. Not a mean match audience; does not cover TV4.

sources.title: RTVE tournament and final outcomes, July 22
sources.notes: 33 television matches average 4.87 million. Final television average 14.5 million excludes separate Play component. Fifty5Blue crossmedia reach has a different denominator and overlap handling.

sources.title: M6 tournament audience release, July 21
sources.notes: Médiamétrie/Médiamat audience to July 20; two fixture averages retained unchanged. 60 million reach uses 4+ and ten consecutive seconds, not a match average.

sources.title: RTVE presidential budget statement, March 27 2025
sources.notes: Primary pre-event cost statement: EUR 1.203 million per match after sharing rights with Mediapro. A budget statement, not an audited realized 2026 fee or proof of unchanged allocation.

sources.title: El País reported RTVE acquisition cost, March 27 2026
sources.notes: Reported EUR 57.5 million including taxes. Gross acquisition context; net sublicense allocation and tax reconciliation unavailable. Do not substitute for E11 per-match budget.

sources.title: Reported M6 fee and audience assessment, July 20
sources.notes: Reports EUR 120 million for 54 matches, expressly not confirmed by M6. Separate from official multi-edition award; no audited territorial/event allocation.

sources.title: M6 third-quarter 2026 financial release
sources.notes: Q3 group EBITA EUR39.0m, +4.2%; video advertising EUR199.2m, +6.2%. Group period outcomes, not isolated World Cup profit. Nine-month programme cost increase is not a rights-fee invoice.

sources.title: FIFA 2027 European coverage agreements, April 21
sources.notes: Complete EBU territorial list resolves the earlier member-list omission: Greenland, Liechtenstein and Luxembourg. Twelve EUR-27 territories in EBU; eight in Saran agency mandate; France direct M6 award. Sweden has both EBU radio-member and direct TV4/SVT references; do not double count.

sources.title: FIFA German 2026/2027 bundled award, June 3 2025
sources.notes: Telekom: all 104 men’s matches in 2026 and all women’s matches in 2027; two U20 editions also included. FIFA retains 30 women’s matches for free-to-air licensing. No disclosed fee allocation.

sources.title: FIFA M6 free-to-air 2026/2030 award
sources.notes: 54 matches in each edition; France, Monaco, Andorra and French overseas territories. Wider territory than FRA-coded swarm, and no disclosed price.

sources.title: RAI 2026 rights award
sources.notes: 35 free-to-air multiplatform matches; at least 32 on Rai1. Non-exclusive radio for all matches. No price disclosed.

sources.title: Reported Italian RAI and DAZN fees, February 28
sources.notes: Secondary reporting citing La Repubblica: RAI EUR110–120m with reported EUR70m non-qualification clause; DAZN EUR35–50m. Pre-event reports, not settled invoices. Do not infer the final amount paid.

sources.title: RAI Norway–England audience, July 12
sources.notes: Rai1 average 4.195 million, 47.4%. One matched fixture; provider/universe not specified in release; no correlation or full-package average.

sources.title: Barlovento July 14 daily ratings
sources.notes: La1-only average 12.716 million, distinct from cross-channel or later consolidated figures. Guests included. Do not pool with RTVE all-channel final as one compatible series.

sources.title: EBU 2027 member announcement, April 13
sources.notes: Nineteen named members map to fifteen countries; the later FIFA list supplies all eighteen territories. Not an all-EUR-27 award.

sources.title: BNT 2026 audience release
sources.notes: Primary BNT release, July 20, verified from downloaded full-page bytes. GARB 4+ final average; same release reports selected fixture averages. Other fixture universes are not separately restated; keep within this publisher group. Website users and tournament reach remain separate.

sources.title: RTÉ semifinal audience release, July 16
sources.notes: Primary discovery lead; full-page web retrieval forbidden. No numeric rank input adopted from the search excerpt.

sources.title: ORF July 2026 audience overview
sources.notes: ORF July overview supplies 52-match coverage and 6.584m tournament reach, 12+. Listed fixture averages are individual halves, so exclude from full-match comparisons. Monthly group audience includes unrelated programming.
